features.statement: A single sans-serif system font stack is used for all text, with no web fonts loaded.
The hero H1 is large, light-weight and centered, with a second line in bold accent color.
Body text is 16px with a roomy 1.6 line-height.
A small uppercase eyebrow label with wide letter-spacing in the accent color sits above the main headline.
Palette is built on one teal hue: dark teal for accent text, mid teal for buttons and bars, with muted grey-teal secondary text.
Section backgrounds alternate between white, pale tint, solid dark accent color bands and a dark footer.
Header is three-part: logo left, primary nav centered, text-only utility links right, with a pale utility bar above.
Hero is text-only, with no photograph: eyebrow, large heading, subtitle and one pill CTA.
Text sections are centered, with a heading, a narrow paragraph about 750px wide, and one CTA.
Product grid shows 12 cards in four columns, each with only a name and price, and no images visible.
Footer has four columns: link lists, contact details, and an email signup, plus a disclaimer and payment icons below a divider.
Secondary CTAs are outlined pills with accent border, accent text and transparent fill.
Cards have thin light-grey borders and medium rounded corners with no shadows.
Product names are bold dark text, and prices are bold accent color pinned to the card bottom.
Header utility links like Search and Cart are text labels, not icons, and the page has no SVG icons.
Newsletter signup is a single simple form: a white input beside an accent-colored Subscribe button.
Category tiles use icons that each get a distinct hue, repeating the logo's motif.
Logo is a small raster image with a lowercase light wordmark.
Decoration is flat: no shadows, blur, animations or transforms, only subtle transitions.
Copy addresses the reader directly as 'you', in a short, warm tone with no em dashes or emoji.
Prices use consistent charm-pricing endings, all ending in .95.
Document title places brand name first, then a pipe separator, then a tagline.
Heading hierarchy skips levels and relies heavily on h3, with h4 only in the footer.
Markup uses landmark elements (header, nav, main, sections, footer) and is link-heavy with many lists.
Styling uses a small set of custom class names, not utility-framework classes, with one stylesheet and one script.
